questions.question: According to the text, what best characterises a use case in requirements specification?

options.A: A detailed code implementation of a feature.
options.B: A description of system performance metrics.
options.C: An interaction description between users and the system using a graphical model and structured text.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] Use cases describe interactions between users and a system using a graphical model and structured text, as stated on [Page 25].

---

questions.question: Which development method first introduced the concept of use cases?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The text notes that use cases were first introduced in the Objectory method (Jacobsen et al. 1993) [Page 25].

questions.question: How can scenarios be employed when proposing requirements for the iLearn system?

options.A: By automatically generating UML class diagrams.
options.B: By facilitating discussions with stakeholders who may have different ways of achieving the same result.
options.C: By performing load‑testing on the prototype.
options.D: By replacing the need for any textual documentation.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Scenarios can be used to propose requirements and to facilitate stakeholder discussions, as described on [Page 19].

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The text states that use cases have become a fundamental feature of the Unified Modeling Language (UML) [Page 25].

questions.question: What primary benefit do use cases provide when describing system requirements?

options.A: They eliminate the need for later testing.
options.B: They offer a graphical model that clarifies user‑system interactions.
options.C: They define the exact database tables to be created.
options.D: They enforce coding standards for developers.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Use cases use a graphical model to clearly depict interactions between users and the system, helping to articulate requirements [Page 25].
